title: How AI Actually Works
subtitle: From neurons to LLMs — demystifying the technology powering the AI revolution
heroTitle: How AI Actually Works

objectives.title: Understand Neural Networks
objectives.description: Visualize how neural networks learn patterns and make decisions through layers of mathematical operations.

objectives.title: Demystify LLMs
objectives.description: Understand how Large Language Models like ChatGPT are built, trained, and how they generate responses.

objectives.title: Connect to Business Value
objectives.description: Identify real-world business applications where neural networks and AI drive competitive advantage.

objectives.title: Build Your First AI Model
objectives.description: Use interactive tools to train your own classifier and experience the AI development process firsthand.

agenda.title: Meeting 1 · Victory Lap: You Trained a GPT
agenda.description: Homework #1 debrief — the loss you watched fall, and the best names from the Canvas thread.
bulletPoints: Loss 3.5 → 1.75: you watched a machine learn, live
Favorite generated names, celebrated properly

agenda.title: Game: Beat Your Own AI
agenda.description: The room vs. the transformer you trained: guess the next letter, then see the model's real probabilities and its surprise when it misses.
bulletPoints: Humans vs. TinyGPT scoreboard, live surprise meter
The reveal: the running surprise average IS the training loss you watched fall

agenda.title: It's Just Numbers: The 104,475-Parameter Census
agenda.description: Where does a model's 'knowledge' physically live? A complete accounting of your model's brain.
bulletPoints: Embeddings, attention, MLPs, head — every number counted
GPT-4 class: same table, ~1.8 trillion rows deep

agenda.title: Interactive: Be the Neuron (Loan Officer)
agenda.description: One artificial neuron = a weighted vote. You set the loan-approval weights by hand — then gradient descent beats you.
bulletPoints: Three sliders: income weight, credit weight, bias
'Let the machine learn' — watch gradient descent roll downhill
Your TinyGPT is 104,475 of these knobs

agenda.title: Hands-On: Open the Hood of Your Model
agenda.description: Colab notebook: retrain your Session 1 model, then X-ray it four ways.
bulletPoints: The map of meaning: your model discovered vowels on its own
The crystal ball: the exact probabilities behind every letter
Attention heatmaps: literally watch it read
'i' wandered off the vowel cluster — and why that matters for trust

agenda.title: Recap + Homework #2
agenda.description: What you now know that most AI users don't — and one honest paragraph for Monday.
bulletPoints: Meaning is location in space
HW #2: which X-ray surprised you most? 3–5 sentences on Canvas, due Thu Sep 24, 11:59 PM

agenda.title: Meeting 2 · HW #2 Debrief + The Pipeline
agenda.description: Your paragraphs, then the question: why can't your name-model hold a conversation? Pretraining → instruction tuning → RLHF.
bulletPoints: Capability, format, manners — where each comes from
Step 1 is your TinyGPT at 10-million-times scale

agenda.title: Game: You Are the Rater
agenda.description: The room becomes the RLHF rater pool: vote between real response pairs, then see what production raters rewarded — and what that did to the models.
bulletPoints: Seven rounds: sycophancy, confident-wrong, over-refusal, length bias, fabricated sources, and more
The reveal: every quirk of the raters became a quirk of the machine

agenda.title: Scale, Economics & the Frontier Map
agenda.description: Why bigger keeps winning, what it costs, and who's who on the September 2026 frontier — with a printable cheatsheet to keep.
bulletPoints: Frontier pricing from $0.75 to $50 per million tokens — and promo pricing that doubles in January
GPT-6, Fable 5.1, Gemini 3.8, Muse Spark, and the open-weights tier

agenda.title: Reading AI Claims: The BS-Detector
agenda.description: GPT-6's launch numbers as a case study — saturation, contamination, harness conditions, relevance, freshness.
bulletPoints: The 37% lab-vs-production gap and the 50x cost variation
Five questions to ask of any AI benchmark claim — screenshot-worthy

agenda.title: Homework #3 + Wednesday Teaser
agenda.description: The model-picker memo: take your week-1 wish, pick the model tier you'd build it on, justify it in 5 sentences.
bulletPoints: Due Thu Sep 24, 11:59 PM on Canvas
Wednesday: Session 3 — your first API key

activities.title: TensorFlow Playground Challenge
activities.description: Navigate to playground.tensorflow.org and complete these three challenges:

steps.title: Warm-up: Circle Dataset
steps.description: Classify the circular data with just 1 hidden layer. How many neurons do you need?

steps.title: Challenge: XOR Problem
steps.description: Why does 1 layer fail on XOR? Add layers until it works. What's the minimum architecture?

steps.title: Competition: Spiral Dataset
steps.description: Race to get the lowest test loss! Screenshot your best result and architecture.

activities.title: Breaking the AI: Jagged Intelligence
activities.description: Test these prompts on ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini. Document where they fail:

codeBlock.code:
1. "How many r's are in the word 'strawberry'?"

2. "What is 47 × 38?" (Don't let it use tools)

3. "Spell 'encyclopedia' backwards"

4. "Count the number of words in: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog'"

5. "Who won the Super Bowl in February 2026?"

activities.discussionNote: Discussion: Why do these fail? What does this tell us about how LLMs "think"?

activities.title: Build Your Own Classifier
activities.description: Use Teachable Machine to train a custom image classifier in 10 minutes:

steps.title: Choose 3 Objects
steps.description: Phone, notebook, pen — or anything around you. You need distinct categories.

steps.title: Collect Training Data
steps.description: Record ~30 samples per class using your webcam. Vary angles and lighting.

steps.title: Train & Test
steps.description: Click "Train Model" and test with new images. What's your accuracy?

steps.title: Reflect
steps.description: What made classification easy or hard? How would this apply to a business problem?

takeaways.text: Neural networks are mathematical functions that learn patterns from data through layers of simple operations.
LLMs predict the next token — they don't "know" things, they simulate plausible text based on patterns.
Business value = pattern recognition — recommendations, fraud detection, forecasting all use these same principles.
AI augments, not replaces — human oversight remains essential for verification and judgment.

homework.label: Watch:
homework.text: Karpathy's "Deep Dive into LLMs" — at minimum, watch 0:00-45:00 (pretraining) and 1:30:00-2:00:00 (hallucinations & psychology)

homework.label: Practice:
homework.text: Get your best score on TensorFlow Playground's spiral dataset. Screenshot your architecture and loss value.

homework.label: Think:
homework.text: Identify one business problem in your area of interest that could benefit from pattern recognition AI. Be ready to share.
